definition_en: to get something into your hands, to carry it with you, or to need a certain amount of time
core_image: 出门前母亲把水壶塞进孩子书包，让他带上
scene: 出门前母亲把水壶塞进孩子书包，让他带上Before leaving, the mother puts a bottle into the child's bag and tells him to take it.
sceneCN: 这里 take 是「拿」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她从书架上拿了那本书。

senses.title: To get something into your hands
senses.definition: To get something into your hands
senses.example: She took the book from the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 她从书架上拿了那本书。
senses.why: Old Norse taka meant to grasp, and English borrowed it with that plain sense.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语 taka 意为抓住，英语借入时保留了这层朴素含义。

senses.title: To carry something with you
senses.definition: To carry something with you
senses.example: Take your umbrella with you.
senses.why: Grasping a thing and carrying it away are two steps of one movement, so the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 抓住并带走是同一动作的两步，于是这个词兼指两者。

senses.title: To need a certain amount of time
senses.definition: To need a certain amount of time
senses.example: The trip takes two hours.
senses.why: If something takes time, it takes it from you as a cost.
senses.whyCN: 若某事取走时间，就是像成本一样从你这里取走。
